title.narrative: UNHCR Flood Mitigation and Hydrology Specialist

description.narrative: UNHCR, in collaboration with the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia’s Refugees and Returnees Service (RRS) and humanitarian partners, is implementing emergency and site development activities for South Sudanese refugees in the Gambella Region. The Luakdong site, covering approximately 1,022 hectares, has been established to host relocated refugees from multiple temporary locations in the Nuer Zone, including Moun and Matar.Technical assessments and site development have highlighted flood risk due to Luakdong’s low-lying topography, proximity to major rivers and poorly drained black cotton soils. Hydrological and hydraulic studies, combined with recent rainy season experience, confirm the need for robust flood mitigation and drainage systems to protect refugees, infrastructure and access routes.In October 2025, flooding and river overflow caused extensive waterlogging and disruption of key services and infrastructure (roads, shelters, hangars, latrines, water points). Refugees and partners were forced to relocate services and shelters to drier areas. Flooding also delayed construction of permanent infrastructure and access roads and increased risks of malaria and waterborne diseases.UNHCR engaged a consultant to conduct flood risk analysis and mitigation design, In June 2025, initially for 330 hectares and later expanded to the full 1,022 hectares of Luakdong. However, the recent flooding and urgent operational needs require additional surge technical support to:• Update and refine flood analysis and mitigation options • Support design and adaptation of dyke, drainage and access road works, including considerations around Nature-based Solutions; and • Provide hands-on technical guidance to flood mitigation activities and measures on the ground and remote.
